notes: Corrected in the phrase *any such evil*. The assimilated article of כַּדָּבָר is a determiner morpheme standing before the word it determines, so rule 41 gives it the quantifying *any* and rule 15's supplied-determiner sentence does not reach the noun; the accepted alignment had marked that article unrepresented and aligned דָּבָר to *any* on the premise that nothing else in the phrase licensed the word.

With *any* placed on the article, דָּבָר and רָע are read as rule 30's generic head noun plus class-naming attributive rendered by the one word *evil*, headed on רָע, rather than leaving the generic noun unrepresented beside it.
*no more* stays split between לֹא and עוֹד because the ASV writes a word for each (rule 35's limit), and the three remaining articles in the phrase are unrepresented under rules 29 and 47.
